channel.title: MYRSS Daily Digest
channel.description: World-affairs digest curated from the latest seven-day repository archive and source RSS feeds, prioritising the past 48 hours. Two articles each from de Volkskrant, New York Times, Follow the Money, Reuters and The New Yorker. Most descriptions rely on RSS metadata; Reuters selections additionally checked against original reporting. Repository source feeds last refreshed around 07:00 UTC on 21 November, so later news may be absent.

item.title: de Volkskrant | FT: Trump wil voor aantreden nieuw Congres in januari akkoord tussen Rusland en Oekraïne
item.description: According to de Volkskrant's headline citing the Financial Times, Trump wants a Russia–Ukraine agreement before the new US Congress takes office in January. Headline-only account; not independently confirmed.

item.title: de Volkskrant | ‘Ergste klimaattop ooit’ eindigt met afsplitsing coalitie klimaatlanden én temperatuurrecord op aarde: 2,1°C
item.description: de Volkskrant's climate summit liveblog headline describes a fractured COP31 outcome and reports a 2.1°C global temperature record. Headline-only account; verify the evolving liveblog for context.

item.title: New York Times | Iraqi Forces Enter Stronghold of Powerful Iran-Backed Militia
item.description: The New York Times RSS summary says Iraqi army and police entered Kataib Hezbollah-controlled territory for the first time in more than a decade. It remains unclear whether the militia will withdraw.

item.title: New York Times | ‘Russian Objects’ Crashed in Poland, Officials Say. Here’s What We Can See.
item.description: The New York Times RSS summary says Polish officials described three incidents involving suspected Russian objects as likely provocations during allied military exercises; no injuries or damage were reported.

item.title: Follow the Money | Zo werd deze oud-Booking-ceo belastingvrij groot­grondbezitter en alternatieve bank in de Achterhoek
item.description: FTM reports that former Booking CEO Kees Koolen used small parcels of land in the Achterhoek in arrangements to acquire farms without paying transfer tax or to assist other farmers. Based on FTM's RSS summary; not independently verified.

item.title: Follow the Money | Hoe land­bouw­kennis uit Wageningen kan bijdragen aan de onderdrukking van Oeigoeren
item.description: FTM reports that Dutch agricultural scientists in Xinjiang cooperate with researchers from the XPCC, a paramilitary organisation implicated in land appropriation and repression of Uyghurs and other minorities. Based on publisher RSS metadata.

item.title: Reuters | EXCLUSIVE: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say - Reuters
item.description: Reuters reports that the US SEC is examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia, according to two informed sources. The scope and timing are unclear; an investigation does not establish wrongdoing. Based on original Reuters reporting.

item.title: Reuters | EXCLUSIVE: Trump official floated ceding Guyanese territory to Venezuela, sources say - Reuters
item.description: Reuters reports that a former Trump administration official floated territorial talks that could give Venezuela partial control of Guyana's Essequibo region. Guyana sought clarification; the US State Department says its border policy has not changed. Based on original Reuters reporting.

item.title: The New Yorker | Three Things to Do This Winter
item.description: Wind-down: The New Yorker daily newsletter recommends winter cultural releases and performances. Based on the publisher's RSS summary.

item.title: The New Yorker | The Look-at-Me Spectacle of Actors Playing Actors in “Elsinore” and “I Play Rocky”
item.description: Wind-down: The New Yorker's cinema review argues that strong performances exceed the conventional filmmaking in two biographical dramas, Elsinore and I Play Rocky. Based on the publisher's RSS summary.
